businessContext: Gap introduced an updated logo on its website and received rapid negative feedback.
strategy: Replace a familiar identity and later invite community participation.
outcomes: Gap announced that it would stop using the new logo and restore the classic identity.
whatWorked: The company reversed the decision quickly and acknowledged process mistakes.
whatFailed: The change underestimated attachment to a distinctive brand asset and community involvement was introduced reactively.
transferConditions: Use when changing a widely recognized identity with accumulated memory structures.
nonTransferConditions: Do not infer that brands can never modernize; test recognition and meaning before replacement.

sources.title: Gap listens to customers and will keep classic blue box logo
sources.methodology: Direct company statement confirms the rollout, response and reversal, but not commercial impact.

rights.notes: Only independently written factual metadata and outbound links are redistributed.

review.notes: Claims checked against the linked primary or regulatory source. Evidence grade remains conservative; independent human review is encouraged.
